newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea Dev Institute lowers GDP growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: Korea Dev Institute lowers GDP growth forecast.

text.p: The government-backed Korea Development Institute (KDI) has revised downward its forecast for this year's real gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 6.0 percent from 6.4 percent, a KDI report said on Thursday.
The institute's earlier forecast was made in December.
Last week the Bank of Korea lowered its GDP growth forecast to 5.5-6.0 percent from 6.4 percent, while the government earlier revised its forecast to 5.5 percent from 6.0 percent.
South Korea's GDP rose by a provisional 7.1 percent in calendar 1996, down from an 8.9 percent rise in 1995.
KDI generally attributed the revisions to fallouts from the collapse earlier this year of two leading steelmakers -- Hanbo Steel Co and Sammi Steel Co.
The KDI report also predicted this year's current account deficit at $19.6 billion, up from its earlier forecast of a $15.5 billion shortfall.
Last year, the current account deficit widened to a record $23.72 billion from an $8.95 billion shortfall in 1995.
The central bank has forecast this year's current account deficit at over $18 billion.
KDI raised its forecast for this year's customs-cleared trade deficit to $11.8 billion from $8.2 billion.
The government has forecast a $14 billion trade deficit for this year, against $20.62 billion in 1996 and $10.06 billion in 1995.
